project: Wuxia Life P7.1 Active Action Experience Closure
description: Close the player-facing experience gaps left after P7 by improving local Web active-action summaries, adding lightweight disturbance narrative cards, clarifying API-mode capability boundaries, strengthening source labeling and reports, and preserving existing build/test/P5/experience/golden-line gates without implementing backend active-action APIs, wiring deferred event files, or expanding into talent, item, region, faction, or worldbuilding systems.

userStories.title: Audit Current Active Action UI Flow
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a read-only baseline of current active-action UI, disturbance handling, continue flow, and API-mode branch so that P7.1 targets real gaps.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory where local active actions are offered
Inventory how action results are displayed
Inventory how disturbance titles are currently surfaced
Inventory how the continue flow returns to planning
Inventory API-mode behavior when no local active actions are available
Produce a short P7.1 UI baseline note
Do not modify business code

userStories.title: Define P7.1 Scope Guardrails
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want P7.1 scope locked so that experience closure does not expand into backend APIs or content wiring.
acceptanceCriteria: Document that P7.1 may improve local Web active-action UI
Document that P7.1 may add lightweight disturbance narrative display
Document that P7.1 must not implement backend active-action APIs
Document that P7.1 must not batch-wire deferred event files
Document required validation commands for closure

userStories.title: Define API Mode Capability Boundary
userStories.description: As a player, I want API mode to clearly communicate whether active planning is supported so that server-backed play does not feel broken.
acceptanceCriteria: Define the player-facing API-mode message when active actions are not supported
Define where the message appears in the Web flow
Document the future backend endpoint boundary without implementing it
Document that local mode remains the P7.1 implementation target

userStories.title: Define Active Action Summary Model
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a focused display model for active-action summaries so that UI can stop relying on a single concatenated text line.
acceptanceCriteria: Define action name field
Define duration field
Define reward summary field
Define cost or opportunity-cost field
Define risk summary field
Define next-step hint field
Typecheck passes if types are added

userStories.title: Render Active Action Summary Card
userStories.description: As a player, I want a readable summary after selecting an active action so that I understand what this period of life accomplished.
acceptanceCriteria: Action result displays as a summary card or equivalent structured block
Summary includes action name, duration, reward, cost, and risk
Summary fits the existing GameScreen visual structure
No broad UI redesign is introduced
Build passes

userStories.title: Test Active Action Summary Without Disturbance
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a deterministic test for a plain active action summary so that result display does not regress.
acceptanceCriteria: Test executes an active action with disturbance disabled or deterministic no-disturbance random source
Test verifies action result summary fields exist
Test verifies duration is shown as short-period progression
Relevant tests pass

userStories.title: Define Disturbance Narrative Model
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a minimal narrative model for disturbances so that random opportunities are visible without becoming full event chains.
acceptanceCriteria: Define disturbance title field
Define disturbance body text field
Define source action field
Define impact summary field
Define return-to-plan hint field
Typecheck passes if types are added

userStories.title: Add Minimal Disturbance Narrative Catalog
userStories.description: As a narrative designer, I want the current minimal disturbances to have lightweight text so that they read as events rather than labels.
acceptanceCriteria: Add narrative text for sparring invitation disturbance
Add narrative text for market rumor disturbance
Add narrative text for minor injury disturbance
Each text is short and returns control to planning
No new disturbance chain state is added

userStories.title: Render Disturbance Narrative Card
userStories.description: As a player, I want a disturbance to appear as a lightweight narrative moment after an active action.
acceptanceCriteria: When a disturbance is resolved, UI displays its title and body text
Disturbance display is visually distinct from the action summary
Disturbance display is visually distinct from formal story events
No full event-chain branching is introduced
Build passes

userStories.title: Return From Disturbance To Planning Flow
userStories.description: As a player, I want to acknowledge a disturbance and continue naturally to the next planning step.
acceptanceCriteria: After disturbance display, continue returns to the existing next-event or action-offering flow
No repeated disturbance loop is introduced
No action result is applied twice
Browser flow is manually verified

userStories.title: Test Disturbance Narrative Paths
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want deterministic tests for disturbance and no-disturbance paths so that lightweight narrative display remains stable.
acceptanceCriteria: Test deterministic no-disturbance path
Test deterministic disturbance path
Test disturbance history remains separate from active action history
Relevant tests pass

userStories.title: Render Progression Source Labels
userStories.description: As a player, I want UI labels to distinguish active actions, random disturbances, and formal story events.
acceptanceCriteria: Active-action summary has a source label
Disturbance narrative has a source label
Formal story events are not mislabeled as disturbances
Labels use player-facing Chinese text
Build passes

userStories.title: Add Report Signal For Disturbance Visibility
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want reports to state whether resolved disturbances were player-visible so that hidden-disturbance regressions are detectable.
acceptanceCriteria: Report data can count resolved disturbances
Report data can count player-visible disturbance narratives
Report flags mismatches between resolved and visible disturbances
Relevant report check passes

userStories.title: Generate P7.1 Closure Report
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want a P7.1 closure report that records what was improved and what remains deferred.
acceptanceCriteria: Report summarizes active-action summary behavior
Report summarizes disturbance narrative behavior
Report records API mode active-action boundary
Report records deferred event files remain out of scope
Report lists validation commands and results

userStories.title: Run Local Browser Acceptance
userStories.description: As a player, I want the local Web flow to prove active action, disturbance, continue, and return-to-planning behavior in the browser.
acceptanceCriteria: Open the local Web app in browser
Start or load a local-mode game
Trigger an active action
Verify action summary is visible
Verify disturbance narrative is visible when deterministic setup produces one
Verify continue returns to normal flow

userStories.title: Run P7.1 Full Regression Gate
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the full known regression set to pass after P7.1 so that experience closure does not break prior gates.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run build passes
npm test passes
npm run gate:p5 passes
npm run gate:experience passes
npm run gate:golden-line passes

userStories.title: Close P7.1 Delivery
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want final delivery notes so the next stage can start from a clear boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: List changed files
List validation results
List residual risks
Recommend whether P8 should start with talents, items, or API active actions
Do not hide API or deferred-content limitations
